name: Kik
seo_title: Is Kik Safe for Kids? Parent's Guide (2026)
seo_description: Is Kik safe for kids? Kik is now for over-18s only, but age checks are weak. The risks of anonymous chat and public groups, and what to do if you find it.
lead: Kik was once a teenage favourite, and it has a long history in grooming cases. It's now meant for adults only. If you find it on your child's phone, here's what you need to know.
answer: No. Kik says users must be 18 or over, and it isn't designed for children. Accounts need only a username and an email address, public groups are full of adult content, and it has no parental controls.

sections.heading: What is Kik?
body: Kik is a messaging app owned by MediaLab. People sign up with a username instead of a phone number, then chat one to one, join public groups found by searching a topic or hashtag, and watch live streams where viewers can send paid donations.
Kik raised its minimum age from 13 to 18 to comply with the UK's Online Safety Act.

sections.heading: Why the age limit isn't enough
body: Kik says it uses an age check provider, VerifyMy, to confirm users are over 18. But children's charities and regulators say checks are easy to get round: sign-up needs only an email address and a date of birth, and neither is checked. In September 2026 the Connecticut Attorney General opened an investigation into MediaLab over how Kik keeps children off the app.

subsections.heading: Anonymous contact
body: Usernames mean nobody has to say who they really are. An adult can easily pose as a teenager, and there's no phone number to trace.

subsections.heading: Grooming
body: Kik has come up in grooming and sextortion cases for years. Offenders use it because it's private and anonymous, and often ask children to move to it from another app.

subsections.heading: Adult content
body: Sexual, drug-related and other adult content is easy to find in public groups and live streams, and much of it seems to get past moderation.

subsections.heading: Spending
body: Live stream donations use credits bought with real money, with some bundles costing hundreds of pounds.

sections.heading: If you find Kik on your child's phone
list: Stay calm: they're more likely to tell you what's happened if they're not in trouble
Ask who they talk to on it, and how they met them
Look together at chats and groups before anything is deleted
Screenshot anything worrying, then block and report
Delete the account and the app, and explain why
after: If an adult has asked for photos, sent sexual messages or tried to meet up, report it to CEOP or the police straight away.

sections.heading: Signs something's wrong
list: A new online "friend" they won't name
Being asked to move a chat from a game or another app to Kik
Gifts, money or credits from someone online
Secrecy about their phone, or panic if you pick it up

sections.heading: What parents can do
body: Treat Kik on a child's phone as a reason to talk, not a reason to shout. The most important question is who asked them to download it. If the answer is someone they met online, that's the warning sign.
list: "Has anyone asked you to chat somewhere more private?"
"If someone online made you feel uncomfortable, would you tell me?"

teachers: If a pupil mentions Kik, ask who suggested it. A request to move from a game, social app or group chat to Kik is a recognised grooming pattern. Record it and follow your safeguarding procedures.

faq.a: 18. Kik raised its minimum age from 13, but sign-up checks are weak and children do still use it.
No. As an app for adults, it has no parental controls. Users can block people, report them and limit messages from strangers.
Because accounts are anonymous, need no phone number and are easy to make, and chats happen away from the apps parents know about.

faq.q: What should I do if my child is on Kik?
faq.a: Talk calmly, look at the chats together, save evidence of anything worrying, then delete the account. Report any adult asking for photos to CEOP or the police.

help: Worried about a child right now? Childline is free and confidential on [0800 1111](tel:08001111), any time. Report suspected grooming to [CEOP](https://www.ceop.police.uk/). You are not alone.
sources: Parent Zone, "What parents need to know about Kik", 11 December 2025
Internet Matters, "What is Kik?" (18+ age limit and VerifyMy checks)
Connecticut Attorney General's investigation into MediaLab, reported September 2026
